summary: Documents the existing SIP private header field P-Charge-Info, used to convey billing information about who should be charged. It has been used in production by vendors and carriers since at least 2007.

plainLanguage.summary: A note on the call says who pays the bill. This writes down how the note is already used.

questions: who pays for a sip call header
how do sip proxies handle billing
subtitle: A SIP header that says who pays the bill for a call.

tldr.problem: In SIP phone systems, the person making a call (shown as Caller ID) may be different from the person who should be billed. Networks need a way to communicate the correct billing party.
tldr.mechanism: The P-Charge-Info header field carries a billing identifier (usually a phone number or SIP URI) that proxies and gateways can use to mark billing records.
tldr.outcome: Used in production by carriers and equipment vendors since 2007 to decouple caller identity from billing identity in enterprise and hosted voice scenarios.

today: RFC 8496 is an Informational specification that documents an existing practice. P-Charge-Info is used in production by carriers and equipment vendors, particularly for enterprise and hosted voice environments.

sections.title: The Billing Identity Problem
sections.content:
In traditional telephony and SIP, the caller's identity (their phone number or SIP address) is often derived from fields like P-Asserted-Identity or From and is displayed to the receiving user as their caller ID. However, in some network configurations, the number shown as caller ID must be different from the number that should be billed.

For example, a large company might want all employees to appear as calling from the main company number, while billing each call to the employee's individual cost center. Or a hosted phone provider might route calls from many customers through shared infrastructure but bill each customer separately.
sections.plainLanguage: Your caller ID shows one number, but the bill goes to a different number. The phone company needs to know which number to charge.

sections.title: What P-Charge-Info Does
sections.content:
The P-Charge-Info header field is a private SIP header that carries billing information. It contains a SIP URI or telephone number that identifies the party to be charged. Several carriers and equipment vendors have used this header in production since at least 2007.

The header is inserted into a SIP INVITE request by one of three entities: the originating proxy, a PSTN gateway acting as a user agent, or an application server. The receiving entity can then use the value in the header to generate accurate billing records without relying on caller identity fields.
sections.plainLanguage: The P-Charge-Info header is just a name or number that says who pays. Networks pass it along so everyone knows the right person gets billed.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
A proxy supporting P-Charge-Info can insert or examine the header in an INVITE request and may decide what billing identifier to use based on local policy. The header contains a name-addr or addr-spec, typically a SIP URI or tel URI. Examples include <sip:+14075550134@example.net;user=phone> or <tel:+14075551234>.

End-user devices (such as a customer's phone) that are not acting as gateways or application servers MUST NOT receive this header for security reasons, since revealing billing information could expose sensitive details or uncover the identity of callers who wish to remain anonymous. Proxies remove the header before forwarding to such devices.
sections.plainLanguage: A proxy looks at the call, decides who should be billed, puts their number in the header, and passes it along. User phones never see it.

sections.title: Real-World Uses
sections.content:
A typical use case is an enterprise where each employee has a direct SIP number but calls go through a corporate proxy. The proxy inserts the employee's number into P-Charge-Info, then sends the call to a SIP service provider. The service provider bills the enterprise for the call and records the employee's number for internal cost allocation.

Another scenario is a large hosted telephony provider with customers distributed geographically. Customers may have local phone numbers, but their calls route through central SIP gateways. The provider can pass a single billing identifier to downstream SIP service providers to simplify billing or to negotiate better rates based on volume.
sections.plainLanguage: A company routes all calls through one gateway, but tells the phone company to charge each call to the right person's cost code.
